tests.name: reads: injected 503s and timeouts are recovered within the retry budget and leave state unchanged
rate limits that never clear stop at the retry budget; the episode call cap is not retried
writes: a response lost after the service committed is never retried, so the effect happens exactly once
writes rejected before reaching the service are also not retried automatically
negative control: a naive retry-everything loop DOES duplicate the write that recovery protects
recovery keeps working against the contract-checked backend (same classes, same invariants)
every registered tool has exactly one recovery class and unclassified or dual-class tools are rejected
the schema cannot be configured to retry writes automatically
transient errors are classified from the registered lists; hard limits and client errors are not transient
reads: transient failures are retried with backoff and counted against the retry budget
retry counts never exceed the budget: the original failure surfaces instead
the per-call attempt cap bounds retries even when budget remains
non-transient read failures are not retried
writes are attempted exactly once, even for transient failures; the outcome is flagged unknown
a definite client rejection of a write is not an unknown outcome and the same write may be tried again
an identical write after a success is replayed, not executed; after an unknown outcome it is refused
backoff is deterministic for a seed, bounded by the registered ceiling, and non-decreasing without jitter
a retry is refused when its backoff would not fit in the remaining elapsed-time budget
aborting the run during backoff stops retrying immediately
a hung attempt is cut off by the per-attempt timeout and retried as a transient failure
model calls retry only listed provider codes and stay inside the same retry budget
run-level budget exhaustion is never swallowed by recovery
the per-call attempt cap also bounds model-call retries when budget remains
a transient read failure is recovered inside the run, counted once in the retry budget and recorded per call
without a recovery policy the TB-015 behavior is unchanged: a transient read failure fails the call
retries stop at the budget and the failure is reported, never hidden
a write whose response is lost is not retried, flagged unknown, and an identical repeat by the model is suppressed
model-call retries share the same budget and a model outage beyond it ends the run with an explicit failure
registered limits are the only source of truth: the run budget file bounds retries for every outcome
killed during a read: the resumed run re-executes the read safely and ends with one final outcome
killed after a write committed but before its response: the write is not repeated and its outcome is reported unknown
a cancellation marker gives a safe abort with a single cancelled outcome and no further effects
killed while paused for approval, with the gateway restarted too: resume completes the approved write exactly once

write_ahead_audit.storage: local APFS volume of the drill host

sensitivity.rule: A run that ended with outcome 'timeout' while one of its model calls was still open at the timeout instant (agent.run start + run.elapsed_ms lies inside that model.call span) ended because the provider did not answer. Before TB-040 these were counted as valid agent timeouts; the corrected runner (src/agent/runner.ts modelInFlight) records them as provider timeouts, so the pair is invalid and excluded.
sensitivity.note: The registered results (TB-032..TB-034) are not rewritten: they were produced and analysed under the protocol as frozen. This is a sensitivity analysis of how much the corrected classification would move them.

invalid_reasons.message: The service could not reach the provider. Try again later.

read_only_storage.session_detail: storage_unavailable: the service cannot record sessions or runs right now; published results are still available
read_only_storage.run_detail: storage_unavailable: the service cannot record sessions or runs right now; published results are still available

not_covered: A checkpoint rewritten together with a recomputed checksum by someone with write access to the run store: the checksum detects damage and naive edits, not a writer who can also recompute it (that needs a keyed MAC with the key outside the store).
Disk-full on the run store (SQLite) itself was not simulated; a read-only audit file and a read-only service volume stand in for a failing disk.
Real provider outages were not induced; the provider faults are a loopback stub reached through the drill hook, which is refused for confirmatory runs.
Memory and CPU exhaustion of the host were not drilled.
